source_refs.title: Make Chrome your default browser
source_refs.section: Set Chrome as your default web browser (Windows 11 steps and installation note)
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11 only; the page gives a note that Chrome must be installed first
source_refs.verified_excerpt: To make sure the change is applied to the correct file types,
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: If you don't have Google Chrome on your computer yet, first download and install Chrome. Select Start. Select Settings, then Apps, then Default apps. Under 'Set defaults for applications,' in the search box, enter Chrome. Select Google Chrome. At the top, next to 'Make Google Chrome your default browser,' select Set default. To make sure the change is applied to the correct file types, review the list under 'Set default file types or link types.'

source_refs.title: Make Chrome your default browser
source_refs.section: Set Chrome as your default web browser (Windows 10 steps, both versions)
source_refs.applicability: Windows 10; the steps differ between the Original version and the Creators Update
source_refs.verified_excerpt: In the 'Choose an app' window, select Google Chrome
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 10: If you don't have Google Chrome on your computer yet, first download and install Chrome. Select Start, and then select Settings. Open your default apps. Original version: select System, and then Default apps. Creators Update: select Apps, and then Default apps. At the bottom, under 'Web browser,' select your current browser. In the 'Choose an app' window, select Google Chrome.
